a_raw: {"translation": "Target defines (without asserting or proving) the following proposition: For all types X and Y, assuming X is nonempty, and for every system N of type S1 X Y (consisting of a finite type N.A1 of nodes, a state type N.A3 n for each node n, an initial global state N.a4 assigning a state in N.A3 n to each node n, a per-node transition function N.a5 taking a node n, a global state (m : N.A1) → N.A3 m, and an input x : X to a next state in N.A3 n, and an output function N.a6 mapping a global state to Y), there exists a system N' of type S1 X Y satisfying three conditions simultaneously: (1) N'.D11: N'.A1 has at least one element, and for every pair of nodes m, n in N'.A1 (including when m = n), there is a nonempty directed chain m = c0, c1, ..., ck = n of length k ≥ 1 such that at each step ci influences c(i+1), meaning there exist two global states σ, σ' of N' that agree on every node other than ci and an input x in X for which node c(i+1)'s update differs (N'.a5 c(i+1) σ x ≠ N'.a5 c(i+1) σ' x); because k ≥ 1 is required even for m = n, every node must have a nonempty path back to itself (for instance, a single node must depend on itself). (2) N'.d13 = N.d13: N'.A1 and N.A1 have the same cardinality (the same number of nodes). (3) S1.D6 N' N: for every finite input list xs : List X (of any length, including the empty list), N' and N produce the exact same output in Y when started at their initial global states (a4), updated synchronously node-by-node left to right on the elements of xs via a5, and evaluated with a6. Notably, N.A1 is not assumed to be nonempty, even though (1) requires N'.A1 to be nonempty and (2) requires N'.A1 and N.A1 to have the same cardinality (so if N has zero nodes, which is possible whenever Y is nonempty, conditions (1) and (2) cannot both hold). Also, N' is not required to have the same node type A1 as N (only the same cardinality), nor is any constraint placed on the node state types N'.A3 (they may be arbitrary types, possibly infinite and unrelated to N.A3)."}
translation: Target defines (without asserting or proving) the following proposition: For all types X and Y, assuming X is nonempty, and for every system N of type S1 X Y (consisting of a finite type N.A1 of nodes, a state type N.A3 n for each node n, an initial global state N.a4 assigning a state in N.A3 n to each node n, a per-node transition function N.a5 taking a node n, a global state (m : N.A1) → N.A3 m, and an input x : X to a next state in N.A3 n, and an output function N.a6 mapping a global state to Y), there exists a system N' of type S1 X Y satisfying three conditions simultaneously: (1) N'.D11: N'.A1 has at least one element, and for every pair of nodes m, n in N'.A1 (including when m = n), there is a nonempty directed chain m = c0, c1, ..., ck = n of length k ≥ 1 such that at each step ci influences c(i+1), meaning there exist two global states σ, σ' of N' that agree on every node other than ci and an input x in X for which node c(i+1)'s update differs (N'.a5 c(i+1) σ x ≠ N'.a5 c(i+1) σ' x); because k ≥ 1 is required even for m = n, every node must have a nonempty path back to itself (for instance, a single node must depend on itself). (2) N'.d13 = N.d13: N'.A1 and N.A1 have the same cardinality (the same number of nodes). (3) S1.D6 N' N: for every finite input list xs : List X (of any length, including the empty list), N' and N produce the exact same output in Y when started at their initial global states (a4), updated synchronously node-by-node left to right on the elements of xs via a5, and evaluated with a6. Notably, N.A1 is not assumed to be nonempty, even though (1) requires N'.A1 to be nonempty and (2) requires N'.A1 and N.A1 to have the same cardinality (so if N has zero nodes, which is possible whenever Y is nonempty, conditions (1) and (2) cannot both hold). Also, N' is not required to have the same node type A1 as N (only the same cardinality), nor is any constraint placed on the node state types N'.A3 (they may be arbitrary types, possibly infinite and unrelated to N.A3).

divergences.description: The author's description claims TARGET asserts a twin with "exactly one more unit" (which would be `N'.d13 = N.d13 + 1`), but the Lean statement actually writes `N'.d13 = N.d13`, requiring the twin `N'` to have the exact same number of units (`Fintype.card`) as `N`. Beyond contradicting the description, this makes `Target` outright false: `N` is quantified over all `S1 X Y` without assuming `Nonempty N.A1`, so for any nonempty `X` and `Y` one can take `N` with 0 units (`N.d13 = 0`), which forces `N'.d13 = 0` and contradicts `Nonempty N'.A1` inside `N'.D11`.

judgement.summary: The description accurately characterizes the passages and most parts of TARGET, but TARGET diverges majorly from the description by stating `N'.d13 = N.d13` (the same number of units) instead of `N.d13 + 1` (exactly one more unit), which also makes the formal statement false for zero-unit systems.
